landing.title: A recorded consultation becomes the proposal it should produce.
landing.lede: Drop in an hour of audio. Shenava writes down the words, tells the two speakers apart, and drafts the proposal under eleven headings — in Persian and English at once. Then it stops and waits for you.
landing.passesTitle: Three passes, each useless without the one before it

pass1.title: The words
pass1.body: Your browser cuts the recording into pieces and sends them one at a time. Each piece is saved the moment it comes back, so a closed tab halfway through an hour loses nothing.

pass2.title: Who said it
pass2.body: A model decides which sentences are the consultant's and which are the client's. It answers with sentence ranges and never rewrites anything, so a wrong answer is only ever a wrong label.

pass3.title: The draft
pass3.body: A model reads the labelled dialogue and writes the proposal as finished sentences, in both languages. It is told never to invent a price, a date or a number — what the meeting left open becomes a question.

landing.modesTitle: Two ways of cutting the audio
landing.modesLede: A transcription request is capped at about 2 MiB. An hour of speech does not fit, so the recording is cut — and how it is cut decides how long you wait.

modeMinute.title: Minute pieces
modeMinute.b: Cut at the quietest moment in the 20 seconds before each minute
modeMinute.c: About 60 requests for an hour of audio

modeLong.title: Long pieces
modeLong.a: 9 minutes per piece, Opus at 24 kbit/s, compressed in your browser
modeLong.b: 1.6 MB per piece — under the cap one raw minute nearly fills
modeLong.c: 6 or 7 requests for an hour of audio

landing.privacyBody: Not in the database, not in object storage, not on disk. Your browser cuts the file locally and uploads one piece at a time to a function that transcribes it and forgets it. The text is kept, deliberately, because the text is the product.
landing.costBody: A few cents to transcribe, fifteen to twenty to draft. Every call is checked against a daily and a monthly ceiling and refused before it is sent if it would go over.
landing.sampleTitle: There is a worked example inside
landing.sampleBody: The seed file ships one complete meeting — transcript, dialogue and draft — so a fresh clone shows the whole product before you have set a single key.

dash.title: Meetings
dash.emptyHint: Run db/02_seed.sql and one worked example appears here.
dash.notReady: The database is not connected yet.
dash.notReadyHint: Open Connections and Shenava will tell you exactly what is missing.

conn.title: Connections
conn.lede: Three things have to answer before Shenava can do anything. Nothing here shows a key's value — only whether it has one.
conn.supabaseWhat: Where the meetings, the transcripts and the drafts live.
conn.openrouterWhat: One key for every model — the transcriber and the writer both go through it.
conn.tablesHow: Open your Supabase project, go to SQL Editor, and run db/01_schema.sql and then db/02_seed.sql.
conn.howBody: Copy .env.example to .env.local and put your values there. The file explains each one. Restart the dev server afterwards — Next.js reads the environment at start.
conn.doorOpen: APP_PASSWORD is empty, so there is no login. That is right on your own machine.
conn.doorClosed: APP_PASSWORD is set, so the dashboard asks for it.
conn.doorWarn: Set it before you put this on a public domain: a public deployment carries your OpenRouter key, and anyone who opens the record page is spending your money.

new.heading: New meeting
new.lede: Choose a recording. Your browser decodes it, cuts it, and shows you the plan before anything is uploaded — the file itself never leaves this page.
new.title: Title

minute.title: Minute pieces
minute.body: 60 seconds each, uncompressed. About 60 requests for an hour of audio, and 12 to 15 minutes of waiting. Right for a short recording.

long.title: Long pieces
long.body: 9 minutes each, compressed in your browser to Opus. Six or seven requests for an hour of audio, and four or five minutes of waiting. Right for a real meeting.
long.unavailable: This browser has no Opus encoder, so it cannot compress the pieces. Safari is the usual case — Chrome or Firefox can.

new.fileNote: Any format your browser can play. Up to three hours. Nothing is uploaded when you choose it.
new.tooLong: That recording is longer than three hours, which is more than the browser can hold decoded. Split it in two and make two meetings.
new.undecodable: Your browser could not decode that file. Try exporting it as WAV, MP3 or M4A.
new.planLine: {duration} minutes of audio becomes {pieces} pieces, sent one after another — about {minutes} minutes of waiting.
new.planBytes: The file is {mb} MB. It stays on this machine; only the pieces are sent, and only as they are needed.
